Name: Dick Crabb
Quirks: talks a great deal — fills silences, offers opinions, tells stories of dubious accuracy
is proud of his local knowledge and his family's name in the way of someone who has little else to be proud of
is honest about his limitations in the calculating way of a man who finds honesty occasionally useful
his cowardice is practical, not shameful to him — survival is the point
is better company than his manner initially suggests — there is genuine warmth under the patter
CharacterDescription:
Nimble Dick Crabb — he goes by Dick, the Nimble is a joke he makes himself — is a small man of no particular house or significance, a native of the Crownlands near the Whispers, a ruined castle on the coast that his family has clung to for generations without the means to maintain it. He is in his thirties, wiry, quick-eyed, and possessed of the particular pride of very minor gentry who are acutely aware of being very minor.

He makes his living as a guide. He knows the Crownlands coast, the roads, the hidden paths, the places where the shore is navigable and the places where it is not. He knows the local smallfolk and the local criminals, which in the Crownlands often overlap. He is useful to people who need to move quietly through territory he knows.

He is not a brave man or a particularly honest one — he will shade the truth for advantage and run from a fight if running seems viable — but he is competent at what he does and surprisingly good company on a long road. He has an opinion about everything and shares it freely and is occasionally right.

He is, at the end of it, a small man trying to get by in a world that does not have much use for him, maintaining his dignity through the only currency available: knowing his particular patch of ground better than anyone else.
AdditionalContext: Campaign context: Dick Crabb is in the Crownlands near the coast, two days before Ned Stark's execution. He is available as a guide to anyone who needs to move quietly through his territory. The war has not yet come to his patch of ground.
